subject: biology
title: Teeth and physical digestion
key_idea: Physical digestion breaks food into smaller pieces without changing its molecules. Teeth cut, tear and grind food, and the stomach churns it. Smaller pieces have a larger surface area, so enzymes can work on them faster.

blocks.text: Digestion breaks food down so that it can be absorbed. This section covers the physical part and why it helps.

items.meaning: The breakdown of food into smaller pieces without chemical change to the food molecules.
The breakdown of large, insoluble molecules into small, soluble ones by enzymes.

items: Physical digestion happens in the mouth, where teeth chew the food.
It also happens in the stomach, where the muscular wall churns the food.
Smaller pieces have a larger **surface area** for the enzymes of chemical digestion to act on.
More surface area means chemical digestion is faster.
Physical digestion makes food pieces smaller. The molecules are not changed.
It increases the surface area for enzymes to act on.

sections.heading: Types of teeth and their jobs

blocks.text: Humans have four types of tooth. Each shape suits a different job in physical digestion.

rows: Flat, with a sharp edge, at the front
Broad and flat, with ridges, towards the back
Large, broad and flat, with ridges, at the back

items: Chewing mixes the food with saliva and makes a ball that is easy to swallow.
The large flat surfaces of premolars and molars give the most grinding.
Incisors bite, canines tear, premolars and molars grind.
Chewing is physical digestion.

blocks.text: A tooth has layers, each with a job. The tooth is held firmly in the jaw.

diagram.alt: The parts of a human tooth: enamel, dentine, pulp, nerves, blood vessels and cement. Tap each part to see its job.
diagram.prompt: Tap a part of the tooth to see what it does.

parts.name: Enamel
parts.detail: The hard outer covering of the crown. It protects the tooth from wear and decay.

parts.name: Dentine
parts.detail: A layer under the enamel. It is softer than enamel and supports it.

parts.name: Pulp
parts.detail: The soft centre of the tooth. It contains the nerves and blood vessels.

parts.name: Nerves
parts.detail: In the pulp. They detect pain and temperature.

parts.name: Blood vessels
parts.detail: In the pulp. They bring food and oxygen to the living cells of the tooth.

parts.name: Cement
parts.detail: A hard layer around the root. It fixes the tooth into the jawbone.

items: The visible part above the gum is the crown.
The root is embedded in the bone of the jaw and is surrounded by the **gums**.
The order from the outside is enamel, dentine, then pulp.
Enamel is the hard outer layer. Dentine lies beneath it.
The pulp holds the nerves and blood vessels.
Teeth are embedded in the jawbone and gums.

blocks.text: The stomach also carries out physical digestion. This section covers how.

items: The stomach wall is made of muscle.
The muscles contract and relax to **churn** the food.
Churning breaks the food into smaller pieces and mixes it with digestive juices.
This increases the surface area of the food for the enzymes.
Muscles in the stomach wall churn the food.
Churning mixes the food with juices and increases its surface area.

checks.a: The breakdown of food into smaller pieces without any chemical change to the food molecules.

checks.q: State why physical digestion makes chemical digestion faster.
checks.a: It increases the surface area of the food, so enzymes can act on more of it.

checks.q: State the name of the hard outer layer of a tooth and the layer beneath it.
checks.a: Enamel is the hard outer layer. Dentine is beneath it.

worked_example.question: Complete the sentences about human teeth. The process of taking food into the mouth is called ______. Flat sharp-edged teeth at the front of the mouth, called ______, are used for biting off pieces of food. The ______ and ______ are the large teeth towards the back of the mouth that are used for ______ the food.
answer_points: Molars and premolars, in either order.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each correct word. Molars and premolars share one mark.
